## TL;DR

Review pass 2 found that touch tap/long-press on card recency hints still opened the Agent drawer or the pipeline task because the browser’s synthesized click followed the tooltip open. This session blocks that click at the source (`pointerup` `preventDefault`) and in capture (`composedPath` + suppression window), and adds component-level regression tests on `TaskCard` and `PipelineCard`.

## Work and rationale

E1 (healthy running cards) landed in earlier rounds: inline “active … ago” and pipeline elapsed text move into `data-tip`, with silent/stuck keeping recency on the line. Pass 2’s blocker was touch-only: `lib/tooltip.ts` correctly pinned the popover on release, but the same gesture activated `@click` on `.tc-hint` (`onCardHintClick` → agent drawer) and on the pipeline `article` (`open`).

The first mitigation (capture-phase click suppression with a short WeakMap window) was necessary but not sufficient. Mobile WebKit and Chromium often still deliver activation unless `pointerup` is cancelled on the same target that opened the tip. Long-press added a second gap: `openFor` runs from a timer while the finger is still down, so release needed its own suppress path.

The final approach is layered: arm suppression when pinning; `preventDefault` on touch `pointerup` when opening from a short tap or when releasing after long-press; `preventDefault` on dismiss tap `pointerdown`; scan `composedPath()` in the capture click handler so bubbling from a `data-tip` child still blocks parent card handlers; and re-create the body tooltip node if tests clear `document.body` while listeners remain installed.

## Approaches tried

Round 2 already added touch open/dismiss and a basic click-suppression test on a bare `button` in an `article`. Review correctly noted that path never mounted Vue `@click` handlers. This session extended `tooltip.ts` and added mounted `TaskCard` / `PipelineCard` cases with `attachTo: document.body`, mirroring board cards.

While wiring those tests, a ordering flake appeared: a pinned tooltip from the TaskCard case caused the next test’s first `pointerdown` to only dismiss the old pin instead of starting a new long-press. Scrolling (the tooltip’s global dismiss signal) after each touch test stabilized the suite.

## Challenges and blockers

Handoff previously failed without an engineering report draft and once on a server-side check timeout; this turn writes the draft before handoff. No human device retest was available here; behaviour is covered by unit/component tests and matches the usual pointerup/click suppression pattern for tooltips on clickable rows.

## Key learnings

Global tooltip delegates should treat “open on touch” and “parent row is clickable” as one interaction design problem: suppress both the synthesized click (`pointerup`) and any bubble-phase card handler (`click` capture over `composedPath`). Isolated DOM fixtures can pass while Vue cards fail, so recency-on-hover acceptance needs at least one mounted card test per clickable trigger.
